subject.title: fix(cron): default deleteAfterRun for isolated cron jobs

question: Should recurring isolated cron jobs be cleanup-safe by default, or should `deleteAfterRun` remain a one-shot-only lifecycle contract?
rationale: This PR and the competing strict-validation PR encode opposite cron lifecycle semantics, and the choice affects existing persisted jobs, future defaults, and session-state retention.

options.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
options.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add an upgrade/load/doctor path for existing omitted persisted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

options.title: Reject recurring delete-after-run
options.body: Choose the strict one-shot-only contract and rework or close this PR after documenting user recovery and caller behavior.

options.title: Accept fresh-create-only default
options.body: Land the new default only for newly normalized jobs while explicitly owning that existing omitted jobs require operator action or separate migration.

recommendation.title: Complete recurring isolated cleanup
recommendation.body: Keep this PR's direction, but add an upgrade/load/doctor path for existing omitted persisted jobs and preserve explicit `deleteAfterRun: false`.

likelyOwner.reason: The unresolved choice spans cron default semantics, SQLite store migration behavior, and compatibility policy, where recent path history points most strongly to steipete.
